correctness.rationale: There are exactly 6,309 nonempty faces, checked by independently structured row-first and column-first enumeration. A deterministic, reproducible 3,105-pair acyclic matching on the face Hasse diagram is fully certified by a 6,309-vertex topological sort of every 27,090 oriented cover edge. Its only critical cells are one 0-cell and 98 4-cells, so integral discrete Morse theory gives an actual CW homotopy model with all attachments constant. The pure dimension-five claim follows from a free-column/free-row-capacity argument. Independent mod-two boundary ranks are corroborative, not an integral inference. Critical calculations and definitions are supplied as an executable standalone certificate; no infinite extrapolation is involved.

originality.rationale: The October 27 2026 paper of Limonchenko and Yu proves a four-row torsion-family homotopy formula for m >= 7 with capacities (2,2,2,m-5); the six-column case (2,2,2,1) is excluded by the explicit bound and by their assumption 6 < m. Their torsion-transfer theorem assumes at least four capacities >= 2, unlike this family endpoint. Rational generalized-chessboard homology formulas and prior connectivity bounds cannot alone imply an integral homotopy wedge of 98 four-spheres. The exact endpoint claim and stronger equivalent formulations were compared in accessible sources; none directly covered it. Residual risk from implicit results, unindexed papers and the incompleteness of ranked searches remains.
residual_risks: Published rational Betti rank 98 may be obtainable from earlier general formulas; only the integral homotopy wedge, not its bare rank, is claimed as new.
A specialized or implicit homotopy argument for the six-column case could exist in unindexed or earlier works not identified by the comparison.
Accessible sections of closest full-text sources were reviewed, not every theorem or appendix of the entire broader literature.

value.rationale: The exact six-column endpoint fills a natural gap in the 2026 four-row torsion family (2,2,2,m-5), which begins at m=7. An integral homotopy decomposition for a pure but nonshellable 5-dimensional complex provides more precise data than homology ranks or torsion-free statements; it separates the m=6 boundary from the onset of known m>=7 torsion without making an artificial infinite-family claim. Its explicit full acyclic matching provides a reusable verification benchmark.
